nodes.t: A map of the whole US that shows where wild clay is likely to be. Tap any spot to see the soil there, how deep the clay sits, its raw colour and how promising it is, with the reasons. Everything else in this diagram is how people come across it, how I keep track of what works, and getting it onto phones.
The places I share clay finds. Each post gets people curious, and the link in it brings them to the map, so I can see which places send people.

Short videos on my account, wildclayhunt: a place worth looking at, then what the map says is under it. Each one is made by the reel maker, the piece that branches off this one. Once I’ve looked a reel over it posts by itself on its day, as a trial reel, which Instagram shows first to people who don’t follow me yet. Next: reading what each one does.

nodes.t: How each reel gets made, built Nov 11. It works from my own phone videos, found by where they were filmed, and asks the map what is under that exact spot. I say yes or no to each reel before it is scheduled. It is set up so my other projects can use it too.
gate: Pick a place from my phone’s video library, by where and when it was filmed
Choose clips no earlier reel has used
Look up that exact spot on the map, and show its screens in the reel
Every line on screen says only what the map says
Keep the sound to footsteps and wind
I look it over, then it is scheduled

nodes.t: Notes on wild clay for every state: the soils the map rates there, where they sit and how promising each one is, with every fact traced to where it came from. The posts here are made from these notes.

My Pinterest, wildclayhunt, where I share wild clay and the places it turns up. From Nov 9 a pin goes out every weekday through June: Virginia one county at a time, and 64 towns across the country known for their clay. Each one opens the map right at its spot. Each pin’s link says what kind of pin it is, so I can see which kinds bring people who look something up. Since Nov 10 every pin is read once a week, on its own: how often it was seen, saved and clicked, and what the people it sent did on the map. The first reading: 5 pins out, seen 19 times, nobody through to the map yet.

nodes.t: Are.na is a site for collecting and connecting ideas. The Georgeville notes are laid out there as a collection, with a link to the map.
The Wild Clay Hunt, my weekly email newsletter about finding clay. 9 issues so far.

A page for each of the 1,239 soil types the map rates, plus a page per state and a guide to finding wild clay, so someone searching for clay near them can land on the map. Since Nov 9 each soil page says the map answers for a particular spot, so AI answers send people there too.

How I keep track of what works: a few numbers, taken by themselves every Monday morning. They help me pick which clay to write about next. Since Nov 10 Pinterest has its own check every Tuesday. Instagram’s reels started going out on a schedule Nov 11; reading each one is next.

Who came, how many looked up a spot, how many upgraded to Pro (the paid version) and where they came from. The 30 days to Nov 9: 302 visitors, 95 looked something up, 7 upgraded, my testers among them. The last week: 148 came and 56 looked something up, against 39 and 25 the week before.
How many people came through each place’s link, so I can see which places send people. Bots and my own visits are left out. Last 7 days: Instagram 28, the plain link 2, Substack 1.

The same count for app downloads, from each store’s own figures. From Nov 9 every iPhone tap on a place’s link carries that place to the App Store, which shows a place once five people have downloaded through it. Google Play’s comes once the Android app is public.
Getting the map onto phones as an app: store listings, screenshots, testers and the steps for release day.
On the App Store since Nov 6, 2026, with Pro as an in-app upgrade. By Nov 7: 16 first-time downloads and the first Pro sale.
The Android version is being tried out by 12 invited potters before it goes public. Google asks for 14 days of testing; theirs began Nov 8, so I can apply to open it to everyone from Nov 22.
The steps for going public, one store at a time.
steps: Nov 6 · The site and every place’s link send iPhones to the App Store.
Nov 6 · An Instagram story and a Substack note.
Nov 5 · A how-to, cut, with a stand-in voice until I record mine.
From Nov 22, when the testers’ 14 days are up and Google approves it.
